_comment: Placeholder content overlay. The real copy lives in content.local.json (git-ignored). Each act pairs the canonical spoken phrase the recognizer listens for with the Title Case video.action it records; aliases are extra phrases that record the same action, for words the small speech model hears differently. Fun Time's overlay lists the same acts under its own acts key, as the queries a voice filter matches against the action recorded here, so the two must agree. cameras lists the camera words, one of which is said and recorded in front of every act: spoken is the canonical phrase, prefix is what it writes in front of the act in video.action (and the backfill grid's column header, and how the prompt scraper cases the same word when a provider names it), aliases are extra phrases that mean the same camera. A camera word that is an initialism, like the example's placeholder XYZ, lists its spelled-out letters as an alias: the small speech model prices each letter as its name, while its one-word form is a guess at a single syllable, so the spelled-out form is the one that actually catches a speaker. A local overlay has to carry this key: a placeholder prefix standing in for a real one would be written into the library's sidecars. Fun Time's overlay lists the same words under its own cameras key, as the words its players set apart from the act on a row, so the two must agree. library_root, chrome_profile and scrape_provider are the machine-specific values the app needs at runtime. Origenerator and the clipper read library_root from their own overlays and the three must agree. project_roots is optional: the folders holding the suite's sibling app checkouts (fun_time, origenerator, clipper, scripture), searched in order, for when those repos do not live under library_root/projects; omit it and that is exactly where they are looked for. retired_root is optional too: where a non-AI original goes once its upscale is made, with its sidecar and funscript beside it. Omit it and the original stays in the library, in its bucket's '2*' folder, which is what the user does by hand; set it to somewhere off the working drive when those folders would otherwise fill it. genau_source names the 0_inbox folder Origenerator drops a looping Genau clip in; it lives here rather than in source because naming a folder inside the library makes that name library vocabulary, which the sanitize blocklist keeps out of a public commit. Origenerator reads the same key from its own overlay and the two must agree. curated_examples is optional: tile label -> the id of the clip that best illustrates it, for the acts the library has no clip tagged with. It names clips inside the library, so it lives here rather than in source; leave it empty and every tile takes the first library clip whose action matches. excerpt_folders is optional: library-relative folders holding scenes carved out of longer videos and nothing else, for the batches that were split before anything recorded a clip block; it is here rather than in source because a folder name is library vocabulary. topaz_ffmpeg and topaz_models are optional: where Topaz Video's own ffmpeg build and its models are, for a machine whose installer put them somewhere other than Program Files and ProgramData. Both upscale stages drive that build and no other, so a wrong path stops the pipeline at its dependency check. version_overrides is optional: stem -> the stem of the video it is a version of, for the version families neither the naming rule nor the pictures can settle (a trim saved under a new name, say), both in one bucket. It is here rather than in source because both halves of a pair are library filenames. display_timezone is optional: the zone a run's timestamps are shown in, e.g. America/Los_Angeles; omit it and they are shown in whatever zone the machine says it is in. warm_gun_outbox names the folder outside the library that Warm Gun still writes its journal to, read alongside the library's own copy; omit it once the app writes into the library. vr_videos is optional: where the library's VR folder is kept when it is not on the library's own drive, a cloud drive say. Their funscripts stay in the library's scripts tree under VR, and the scripts stage matches a script against them as though they sat in the library; omit it and the VR videos are looked for in the library itself.
